# `silk/concurrency/local_scheduler`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A deterministic, single-threaded scheduler for structured Fibers.

## When to use
Use [`LocalScheduler.execute`](#LocalScheduler.impl.execute) at the application entry to run one lazy program that uses the
`Scheduler` and `MonotonicClock` services. For parallel work on several threads, use
`silk.concurrency.thread_pool`.

## Details
Each call makes new task storage, a FIFO ready queue, and a private timer source. The root is
task zero, and uses the same `Execution<()>` storage as each child.

A clock wait in a task parks only that task. When no task is ready, the driver waits on the
parent `MonotonicClock` for the earliest timer. [`LocalScheduler.execute`](#LocalScheduler.impl.execute) returns only after
the root finishes, and it cancels each unfinished descendant first.

## Errors
- The typed failure of the root program.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if task storage cannot be allocated.
- [`StalledError`](#StalledError) if no task is ready, no timer is waiting, and the root is not finished.

## Examples
### Run a root program
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.concurrency.fiber { Cancelled, Fiber }
import silk.concurrency.local_scheduler { LocalScheduler, StalledError }
import silk.system.monotonic_clock { MonotonicClock }
import silk.system.monotonic_clock_native { OsMonotonicClock }
import silk.concurrency.scheduler { Scheduler, TaskIdExhaustedError }

effect fn square(value: i32) -> i32 {
  // Lets the other ready task run first.
  run Fiber.yieldNow()
  return value * value
}

effect fn root() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError | TaskIdExhaustedError | Cancelled
  ? &mut Scheduler | &mut MonotonicClock {
  let three = run Fiber<i32, never>.forkChild(square(3))
  let four = run Fiber<i32, never>.forkChild(square(4))

  // join parks the root until the child finishes.
  let first = run three.join()
  let second = run four.join()
  if first + second != 25 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError | TaskIdExhaustedError | Cancelled | StalledError {
  let mut clock = OsMonotonicClock.make()
  let mut scheduler = LocalScheduler.make()
  return run scheduler.execute<i32, OutOfMemoryError | TaskIdExhaustedError | Cancelled>(root())
    |> Effect.provideMut<MonotonicClock>(&mut clock)
}

effect fn failed<E>(error: E) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 1
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), failed)
}
```

A deterministic, single-threaded `Scheduler` provider for structured Fibers.

### When to use

Use [`LocalScheduler.execute`](#LocalScheduler.impl.execute) at the application entry to run one lazy program that uses the
`Scheduler` and `MonotonicClock` services. For parallel work on several threads, use
`silk.concurrency.thread_pool`.

### Details

Each call to [`LocalScheduler.execute`](#LocalScheduler.impl.execute) makes new task storage, a FIFO ready queue, and a

<a id="LocalScheduler.impl.execute"></a>

### Method `execute`

```silk
pub effect fn execute<A: 'static, E: 'static>(
    self: &mut Self,
    program: once Effect<'static;
      A
      ! E
      ? &mut Scheduler | &mut MonotonicClock
    >,
  ) -> A
  ! E | OutOfMemoryError | StalledError
  ? &mut MonotonicClock
```

Runs one lazy root program under this scheduler and returns its result.

#### Details
The root becomes task zero. This call owns all task and timer storage of the run. It gives
each task its own `Scheduler` and `MonotonicClock` clients, and runs ready tasks in FIFO
order.

A clock read in a task uses one cached mark per driver turn. A wait suspends its task. Tasks
resume in deadline order, then in registration order. When the ready queue is empty, the
driver waits on the parent `MonotonicClock` for the earliest timer.

Before it returns or fails, it cancels each unfinished descendant and releases the run state.

#### Errors
The failure of the root, `OutOfMemoryError`, or [`StalledError`](#StalledError) when no task is ready and no
timer is waiting.

<a id="LocalScheduler.impl.start"></a>

### Associated function `start`

```silk
pub effect fn start() -> LocalDriver
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut MonotonicClock
```

Starts a caller-driven [`LocalDriver`](#LocalDriver) with no root task and an empty ready queue.

#### Details

Tasks added with [`LocalDriver.spawn`](#LocalDriver.impl.spawn) share one scheduler, FIFO ready queue, and timer table,
and advance only when the caller invokes [`LocalDriver.step`](#LocalDriver.impl.step) or [`LocalDriver.driveOne`](#LocalDriver.impl.driveOne).

<a id="LocalDriver"></a>

## `LocalDriver`

```silk
pub struct LocalDriver
```

A caller-driven, non-blocking handle to a [`LocalScheduler`](#LocalScheduler) instance.

### When to use

Use [`LocalScheduler.start`](#LocalScheduler.impl.start) and [`LocalDriver`](#LocalDriver) when a host event loop (such as a UI loop
waiting on external wakes and OS events) drives fibers in bounded turns instead of handing
control to [`LocalScheduler.execute`](#LocalScheduler.impl.execute) until completion.

### Details

Unlike [`LocalScheduler.execute`](#LocalScheduler.impl.execute), [`LocalDriver.step`](#LocalDriver.impl.step) never blocks waiting on timers and never
raises [`StalledError`](#StalledError) when parked tasks wait for external `Execution.wake` calls.

Spawns a new top-level task onto this driver and enqueues it for execution.

#### Errors

Fails with `OutOfMemoryError` on allocation failure, or `TaskIdExhaustedError` if the
scheduler's task identity space is exhausted.

<a id="LocalDriver.impl.cancel"></a>

### Method `cancel`

```silk
pub fn cancel(self: &mut Self, target: TaskId) -> ()
```

Synchronously cancels `target` and all of its unfinished descendants.

#### Details

Parked executions are dropped immediately, running their `Drop` hooks and non-parking
finalizers and completing their [`Fiber`](./concurrency-fiber.md#Fiber) observers as cancelled. Calling `cancel` on an
already finished or cancelled task is a no-op.

```silk
pub effect fn step(self: &mut Self, maxActivations: usize) -> StepResult
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut MonotonicClock
```

Advances due timers and runs up to `maxActivations` ready tasks without blocking.

#### Details

Never sleeps waiting for timers and never raises [`StalledError`](#StalledError) when live tasks wait for
external wakes.

<a id="StalledError"></a>

## `StalledError`

```silk
pub struct StalledError
```

Reports that no task is ready and no event registration remains while the root is incomplete.

### Details

[`LocalScheduler.execute`](#LocalScheduler.impl.execute) raises it when no task is ready, no timer is waiting, and the root is
not finished. It cancels and releases the incomplete task tree before it raises this error.
